Quick triage notes after scanning the attached traces and recent deploys:

What I see:
- There was a config push at 2027-04-07T02:14:22Z that adjusted the kv-routing policy (shard weights) and increased default coalescing batch_size from 32->96 on the affected pool.
- Trace sampling shows long head-of-line blocking: single requests with large prefix cache misses cause the serving runtime to keep a GPU lane occupied while subsequent small requests queue behind it.
- Several boxes show repeated KV lookup timeouts (200–500ms) on the same logical shard index. The shard map shows heavy skew — some KV shards are 3–5x hotter.

Prelim hypothesis: the routing weight change + larger coalescing batch increased variance in per-lane request cost. Hot shards are getting mapped to lanes that then accept big coalesced batches, which causes HOL blocking and downstream timeouts — the behavior looks like cache thrash + lane starvation.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered by risk):
1) Roll back coalescing batch_size to 32 for the production lane (fast, low risk).
2) Temporarily pin hot KV shards to additional replica lanes (requires shard rebalancing; ~20m), which should reduce single-lane hotness.
3) Failover customer to older model variant without large prefix cache dependence (more noise for Atlas).

I'll package the exact commands and safe rollback steps. Attaching kv-shard-map snapshot and a short trace snippet.

Subject: Post-incident: Atlas P1 summary & action items (SUP-4981)

Summary:
- Incident window: 2027-04-07T07:46 PDT — 2027-04-07T10:02 PDT
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 and ~6% 5xx for Atlas v-prod (US-west).
- Root cause (short): combined config drift that increased coalescing batch_size + unintended KV shard weight change caused severe shard skew and HOL blocking on GPU lanes leading to cache thrash and timeouts.

Actions taken during incident:
- Rolled back batch_size 96->32 at 09:45 PDT (canary then global rollout) — immediate improvement in p95 within 8 minutes.
- Applied temporary shard pinning for top-3 hot shards to reduce variance (20m window).
- Deployed a short-term runtime guard that prevents coalescing batches above 48 when shader-hotness > 2.5 (safety throttle).

Follow-ups / owner list:
- David: permanent shard rebalancer tuning + automated detection for shard skew (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Marcus: improve canary rollout policy to detect HOL patterns earlier (ETA: 1 week)
- Chloe: update customer-facing postmortem and review change controls with Atlas (ETA: 3 business days)

Related items: JIRA SUP-4981 created for the follow-ups. Attached artifacts and the exec briefing are in the Drive link.

Attachments: [logs_20270407.tar.gz, kv-shard-map-20270407.json, exec-briefing-atlas-4x7.pdf]

Thanks for the partnership and patience while we resolved this. We'll follow up with a full RCA doc and proposed controls to prevent repeat.
